notes.summary: Repaired finite-PA contact/circuit theorem: the strict-floor equivalence explicitly requires a PA PC germ. Noncontact forces a flat relation; compatible positive-mass flat germs yield exact roof obstructions. This covers finite PA endpoints only.
notes.detailedSummary: On finite pure positive balanced rational embedded spaces, literal integral-slope/rational-constant PA and real PA on finite rational complexes are treated separately. Fixed-structure PC conditions are rational circuit inequalities. Under the necessary PC/nonnegative-cost hypothesis, absence of zero-cost positive relations gives a strict affine floor. The corrected necessity theorem and converse roof establish a finite-PA endpoint equivalence. Whole247 remains FAIL and is preserved.
notes.text:
The failed whole247 statement is materially repaired, not relabeled. On the unit balanced line, gamma=|x| and f=-|x| on |x|<=1, f=|x|-2 outside, give bounded relative literal PA. At zero its slopes are (-1,-1), K={(a,a):a>=0}, and all nonzero costs are -2a. There is no zero-cost relation, but a strict floor bx would require b<-1 and b>1. Thus the corrected floor lemma explicitly assumes PA PC, equivalently nonnegative cost on every positive tangent relation. The old source, argument, ledger, FAIL report and native unknown-support failure remain preserved.

Here is the reconstructed finite theorem. On a finite pure positive balanced rational X in N_R, for a continuous PA function f and rational face center p, choose nonzero rational generators d_i of all incident tangent cones, including opposite lineality generators. Set U=(d_i), s_i=h_p(d_i), K={lambda>=0:U lambda=0}. A flat relation is nonzero lambda in K with s.lambda=0. At every face, f is PC exactly when s.lambda>=0 on K. Necessity uses rational endpoints p+epsilon d_i with common small rational epsilon and normalized relation coefficients. For sufficiency, T=R_+^m+image(U^T) is a closed finitely generated cone: eliminating dependent active columns leaves an independent subset, whose inverse bounds coefficients; there are finitely many subsets. If s is outside T, nearest-point separation gives lambda>=0, U lambda=0, lambda.s<0. Hence s=U^T ell+b, b>=0, giving a linear local support. The generator test works throughout each face's relative interior. Local supports imply convexity on every contained segment: a positive maximum after subtracting its chord would have supporting slope zero, making its maximum set open as well as closed, contradicting endpoint values. Propagating the center support along each incident endpoint segment and summing proves every PCC inequality, without identifying PC with ambient-global convexity.

Extreme rays of K have one-dimensional kernel on their positive support: otherwise a small two-sided independent kernel perturbation breaks extremality. Their supports have at most rank(U)+1 elements; rational elimination supplies finitely many circuit generators. This gives finite rational PC inequalities on each specified carrying structure.

The caller B225 positive-spanning theorem applies to inherited finite positive balanced stars, with saturated tangent lattices and unchanged primitive quotient classes. Thus the normalized section K intersect {sum lambda=1} is nonempty compact. With the corrected PC hypothesis, no flat relation makes every normalized cost strictly positive; its minimum theta is positive. Apply the preceding separation to s-delta 1, 0<delta<theta, giving generator residuals >=delta. For a cone vector x=sum a_i d_i, the residual is >=delta sum a_i >=delta ||x||/max_i||d_i||. This is the strict affine floor. Opposite lineality generators force a flat relation.

If the actual envelope f=P_gamma(u) is finite PA and noncontact at v for bounded continuous u, it is PC by supremum Jensen inequalities. A continuous positive obstacle gap persists near v. If no flat relation existed, raise f locally to max(f,f(v)+t+ell(x-v)), with t less than both the gap and the strict-floor collar margin. It agrees with f on the collar, stays below the obstacle and preserves growth. Supports of active entries persist, including ties, so this is an unrestricted PC competitor raising f(v), contradiction. No PA or operator assertion is made for the inserted floor.

Conversely let gamma and f be PA PC in the same coefficient category, with f-gamma bounded, and a flat relation at a rational vertex v of positive raw atom m_v. Choose rational R>0 so its closed sup-norm ball is in f's affine star and excludes other carrying vertices. Let B=(R-rho(x-v))_+ and u=f-gamma+B. It is bounded PA in the chosen category; B is literal. For flat relation lambda,d_i use rational boundary endpoints y_i=v+R d_i/rho(d_i), coefficients beta_i=lambda_i rho(d_i)/R. Their normalized barycenter is v and average f-value is f(v). Every printed-PC competitor q therefore has q(v)<=f(v). Rational radial chords give q<=f inside; outside the roof the obstacle gives q<=f. Shrinking rational simplices in the minimal rational face extend the bound to real points without continuity of q. Therefore the unrestricted envelope is f, already PA and regularizable by a constant sequence. Refinement creates no artificial atoms, and the contact integral is exactly -R m_v.

The genuine raw measure uses saturated primitive inward normals and D_f c(tau)=sum c_sigma f_sigma(n_sigma/tau)-f_tau(sum c_sigma n_sigma/tau), iterated d times, with no additional factorial. The complete frozen publisher BBGS Definitions 3.2–3.9, Proposition 3.12, Proposition 3.15, Lemma 3.18 and Proposition 3.19 were independently checked. Embed x as (x,1). If a_sigma is tangent lattice covolume, saturation gives projected primitive height a_sigma/a_tau. Euclidean weights a_sigma c_sigma are balanced; BBGS's negative product applied to -f has coefficient a_tau D_f c. Tangent slopes cancel by continuity and balancing. Repeat at every recursive dimension, a_vertex=1. The commutativity proof pairs the two boundary facets of each codimension-two wedge using reflected unit perpendiculars, with coefficients -cot(theta), csc(theta); symmetric diagonal and exchanged cross terms give equality. Subdivision retains old facets, cancels opposite normals in old affine cells and assigns zero inherited weight in higher-dimensional old cells. Linear-form annihilation proves balanced preservation. These proofs apply to real and zero intermediate weights; local supports give positivity at each step.

Consequently all admissible PA obstacles with finite relative PA envelopes have zero contact iff every actual relative PA PC function satisfies m_v>0 implies no flat relation. On a fixed structure, shared-face equations, circuit PC inequalities, equality of actual recession slopes, zero extreme-relation cost and a positive degree-d raw mass polynomial give the exact real semialgebraic obstruction disjunction. Literal feasibility additionally requires integral tangent slopes and rational constants. Neither one structure nor this theorem bounds all refinements or covers non-PA endpoints.

notes.detailedSummary: The saturated unit-weight plane sum has a positive-growth literal reference and actual relative literal PA endpoint. notes.text:
Let X={y=0} union {x=0} in Z^3_R with [X]=[P_xz]+[P_yz]. Each coordinate plane lattice is saturated; top cells have unit weight. Opposite primitive quotient normals balance each plane; at the shared z-axis the sum of +/-e_x,+/-e_y is zero. Raw linearity gives D_f^2[X]=D_f^2[P_xz]+D_f^2[P_yz]. This is sum-cycle additivity, not product separability.

Gamma=max(|x|,|y|,|z|)+|z| and f=max(|x|,|y|-1,|z|)+|z| are actual ambient convex restrictions, literal PA with rational walls. Every printed PCC Jensen inequality holds. Shifting one maximum entry gives -1<=f-gamma<=0. Gamma>=rho=max(|x|,|y|,|z|), so all nonzero recession slopes are positive.

In plane coordinates (a,b), h=max(|a|,|b|)+|b| has first cycle weight 2 on the two a-axis rays and 1 on four diagonal rays (s,t), s,t=+/-1. Axis gradients (s,1),(s,-1) with transverse lifts +/-(0,1) give 2. Diagonal outer/central gradients (s,t),(0,2t) have difference (s,-t); tangent (s,t), transverse lift (s,0) have determinant +/-1, and evaluation gives 1. Along the nonzero b-axis both gradients are (0,2t), hence weight zero. These exhaust the six affine forms a+b,a-b,-a+b,-a-b,2b,-2b. At zero the weighted directions balance; outgoing slopes are 1 on axes and 2 on diagonals, yielding mass 2+2+4*2=12.

On P_yz, g=max(|y|-1,|z|)+|z| has first cycle weight 4 on central z=0, -1<=y<=1, weight 2 on outward y-axis rays from p_s=(0,s,0), and weight 1 on rays from p_s in directions s e_y+/-e_z. Central gradients (0,2),(0,-2) give 4; outward gradients (s,1),(s,-1) give 2; diagonal gradients and primitive lifts give 1 as above. Other artificial y=+/-1 walls and the nonzero z-axis have identical gradients and zero weight. At p_s, directions -s e_y,s e_y,s e_y+e_z,s e_y-e_z have weights 4,2,1,1 and slopes 0,1,2,2. Their weighted sum is zero and second mass is 6. Subdivision of the central segment at zero adds opposite weight-four y directions of zero slope, hence zero vertical atom. Thus MA(f)=12 delta_0+6 delta_p++6 delta_p-. Gamma has h on both planes, hence MA(gamma)=24 delta_0. There is no extra factorial; gradient polygon areas 6,3,3 are independent checks only. Equal totals 24 do not prove contact.

For R=1/4 set B=(R-rho)_+, u=f-gamma+B. The flat rational endpoints (0,+/-R,0) have f=B=0, forcing q(0)<=0 for every printed-PC competitor below f+B. Each rational interior point has its radial boundary chord in an incident homogeneous linearity cell of f, forcing q<=f. Outside the roof this is the direct obstacle bound. Shrinking rational simplices give the real-point bound without assuming competitor continuity. Therefore P_gamma(u)=f, its usc regularization is itself, and it is genuinely literal and real regularizable. New walls inside affine top cells have cancelling first weights; new vertices on straight affine first edges have cancelling second slopes, so no artificial mass occurs. Only the origin is in the roof; the integral is -(1/4)*12=-3.

The precise excluded decomposition is f(q,z)=F(q)+H(z) on the original cross C times the z-line. At horizontal corners (x,z)=(0,0),(R,0),(0,R),(R,R), f and gamma values are 0,R,2R,2R, mixed difference -R. Obstacle values are R,0,0,0, mixed difference R. No universal reparametrization exclusion is claimed. The old endpoint max(|x|,|y|-1,0)+|z| was separable and is not relabeled.

Exact finite evidence: 20 active triples per six-form plane, six and seven positive first edges, all primitive balances and recursive atoms passed; 3,321 rational grid points and 90 interior radial chords passed. Polygon checks are independent of the operator proof. Artifacts: coupled-section.tex, check_certificates.py, evidence/certificate-output.json. Rerun: python check_certificates.py. No all-obstacle pair regularity follows.

notes.summary: Actual-reference realization of finite local PC jets in the real category for rational-affine positive-growth references. Every local flat positive-mass real jet has a rational realization. This removes global compatibility only in that finite-PA scope.
notes.detailedSummary: A slow ambient rational norm is raised above the actual reference, then a small scaled PC local jet is inserted with a strict collar. Its germ, flat relations and scaled raw mass are preserved. Rational approximation within the fixed circuit cone retains zero extreme cost and positive mass. The resulting finite-PA contact criterion is local geometry, still quantified over all rational refinements; arbitrary irrational references and non-PA contact are not classified.
notes.text:
Fix the actual rational-affine PA PC reference gamma on finite positive balanced embedded X, with positive growth, and a rational point v. Let h be a continuous homogeneous rational-coefficient PA PC function on a specified finite rational refinement of its tangent star, h(0)=0. Its finite slopes give |h(x)|<=L rho(x). Positive growth plus vertex/recession decomposition gives gamma>=a rho-b for a>0. Choose rational epsilon>0 slower than every reference recession slope, rational C>gamma(v), and Psi=max(gamma,C+epsilon rho(x-v)). This is real PA on a finite rational structure, has local supports, equals the second entry near v and differs boundedly from the actual gamma.

Choose a rational star radius r where X is exactly its truncated tangent star; take rational delta>0 with delta L<=epsilon/2 and rational 0<t<epsilon r/4. Inside the ball set G=max(Psi,C+t+delta h(x-v)); outside set G=Psi. On the collar r/2<=rho<r, epsilon rho>=t+delta h, so the definitions agree. Near v the raised jet is active, giving exactly germ C+t+delta h. Supports of active entries support the maximum, also at ties; the collar adds no defect. The global support proof from n1 gives every PCC inequality. All fan, ball and equality walls are rational; G is relative real PA PC with bounded difference from the actual reference. Its raw atom is delta^d m_0(h) and flat relation costs scale by delta. This is real-category gluing, not literal gluing.

For any real-coefficient bad jet on that fixed fan, n1's shared-face and PC conditions are rational linear constraints. A flat relation has zero cost on some rational extreme relation because every extreme cost is nonnegative. Adjoin that rational zero-cost equation. Rational feasible points are dense even on the boundary: solve active rational equalities in a rational affine basis and approximate, preserving inactive strict inequalities. The raw mass polynomial is continuous, so strict positivity persists in a close rational feasible jet. The preceding construction realizes it globally. This also works with specified positive real top weights, since the mass polynomial remains continuous; actual weights and saturated normals are retained.

Thus, for rational-affine positive-growth gamma, real contact for all bounded real PA obstacles whose actual envelopes are finite PA is equivalent to: at every rational point and every rational tangent-star refinement, every PC homogeneous PA jet with a flat relation has zero raw top atom. Sufficiency applies this local condition to each positive-mass finite envelope vertex and uses n1's noncontact theorem. Necessity realizes a bad jet by G and applies n1's exact roof obstruction. The criterion is structural within this finite sector and contains no unexplained global extension premise. It is not the entire original classification: no refinement bound, arbitrary irrational-reference gluing, all-obstacle regularization, or non-PA contact sufficiency is proved.

Finite corroboration used the coupled space with epsilon=1/8, delta=1/32, t=1/256, r=1/4 and h=max(|x|,|z|)+|z|, checking 3,321 grid points and the collar. The scaled origin atom is 12 delta^2=3/256. These finite lists corroborate the continuum proof only. Artifacts: jet-section.tex and evidence/certificate-output.json. Rerun: python check_certificates.py; python rebuild_paper.py.

notes.summary: New sequence-independent uniform extension of genuine raw mixed MA on the regularizable domain for rational-affine positive-growth references. This covers non-PA regularizable endpoints, but not arbitrary continuous PC envelopes or irrational references.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite edge integration by parts and degree cancellation, rational compact PA test decomposition into relative PC differences, and a truncated-reference moment bound prove existence, independence, total mass, uniform continuity and locality. Literal and real approximation domains are separately retained. No BMPS general extension or density theorem is imported; rational-reference closure is an explicit limitation.
notes.text:
Assume finite pure positive balanced embedded X and rational-affine PA PC gamma positive at infinity. Literal references qualify; arbitrary irrational PA_R references are excluded from this result. Let M=deg(gamma) for the actual raw recursion proved in n1.

On any intermediate balanced one-cycle Z, bounded PA functions b,c have zero slopes on unbounded edges. Each bounded primitive-length-L edge [v,w] contributes Z(e)(b(v)-b(w))(c(w)-c(v))/L to integral b D_c Z, symmetrically in b,c. Also deg(D_b Z)=0 by cancelling bounded outgoing slopes and zero unbounded slopes. Replacing each relative mixed PA factor by gamma therefore gives common mass M. Local supports give nonnegative mixed measures.

For a compact ambient rational-affine PA test psi, collect rational wall forms L_j and choose rational K so H=K sum |L_j| and H+psi are ambient convex: at every generic crossing the positive 2K bend dominates the finite negative bend of psi, and continuity covers all segments. Positive growth gives gamma>=a rho-b. Choose rational epsilon so epsilon H is slower at infinity, and rational C so C+epsilon H dominates gamma on a neighborhood of supp(psi) intersect X. Then theta0=max(gamma,C+epsilon H), theta1=theta0+epsilon psi are rational-affine relative real PA PC. Near the support theta1=C+epsilon(H+psi); outside it is theta0. These descriptions give local supports. The slower term is inactive outside a compact set. Thus theta1-theta0=epsilon psi, without irrational carrying walls. They need not be literal, but their finite real raw measures are already proved.

Such tests are uniformly dense in C_c(X): for positive compact continuous g use finite rational nets and rational heights in max_j(a_j-L rho(x-v_j))_+, choosing integer L and a fine net from a uniform-continuity scale. Bumps farther than that scale vanish; nearer bumps differ by at most continuity and sampling errors. A fine enough net gives the reverse approximation bound. Subtract approximants to g_+ and g_- for signed g. This asserts no density in all C_b.

For two relative PA PC tuples a,b, telescope one factor at a time. The other factors form positive balanced one-cycles Z_i. Edge integration by parts gives integral psi D_(a_i-b_i) Z_i = integral (a_i-b_i) D_psi Z_i. Since D_psi=(D_theta1-D_theta0)/epsilon and each positive mixed measure has mass M, total variation is <=2M/epsilon. Therefore |integral psi (MA(a)-MA(b))| <=(2M/epsilon) sum_i ||a_i-b_i||_infinity. Uniform-Cauchy approximants have Cauchy integrals on the dense tests and then on C_c by the common mass bound. The limiting positive functional defines a unique Radon measure: open-set mass is the supremum of functional values on compact continuous tests between 0 and 1; open covers and finite partitions prove subadditivity, disjoint tests prove addition, metric separation gives Borel measurability, and range-step approximation proves the integral representation. The manuscript supplies these construction details.

Mass does not escape. Shift gamma by a rational constant to be nonnegative and let ||a_i-gamma||<=C uniformly. The rational-affine q_j=max(gamma-j,0) are relative PC. Bounded-difference integration by parts reads integral(gamma-q)MA(a1,...)=integral(gamma-a1)MA(q,...)+integral(a1-q)MA(gamma,...). Splitting the latter term into a1-gamma and gamma-q and iterating gives integral min(gamma,j)MA(a)<=2d C M+integral gamma MA(gamma)=K. The reference measure has finite support, so K is finite. Increasing j gives integral gamma MA(a)<=K, hence uniform tail mass <=K/T on {gamma>T}. Properness gives tightness; compact cutoffs prove limiting mass M and convergence for every bounded continuous test.

The same test estimate between arbitrary approximants proves sequence independence and uniform continuity. For locality, a compact test in an open equality set has D_psi supported there; its bounded-variation estimate uses only local approximation error, tending to zero. Symmetry passes from raw symmetry. The domain is exactly uniform completion of relative PAPC_Z or, separately, PAPC_R. Extracting approximants with error 2^-n and adding rational constants 4*2^-n makes them decreasing, so this is the stated regularizable domain. No operator is assigned merely from continuity. The literal operator is the uniquely determined continuous completion of the actual source raw formula; the real one is explicitly constructed here.

For actual bounded continuous obstacles converging uniformly, if their envelopes lie in this proved domain, R230 applies on finite positive balanced X with continuous reference and gives envelope uniform convergence. Their continuous bounded gaps then have convergent exact contact integrals by this operator theorem. This stability does not prove missing domain membership of general envelopes. notes.summary: Unconditional non-PA real-regularizable coupled envelope: an explicit quadratic transition produces a genuine extended measure on two segments and four parabolic arcs, plus origin mass 12, and contact -3. It is not literal-regularizable.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual reference is the coupled literal gamma from n2. Dyadic rational chord approximants give real PA regularization with error 1/(8N^2), exact raw atom weights and a Riemann-sum measure limit independent of the sequence by n4. The continuous roof obstacle has unrestricted envelope F, including discontinuous competitors. This obstacle is not PA; no all-obstacle regularity theorem follows. A 3/64 quantization gap excludes the literal domain.
notes.text:
Keep X,gamma from n2. Let a(y)=0 for |y|<=1, (|y|-1)^2/2 for 1<=|y|<=2, and |y|-3/2 for |y|>=2. It is even convex, with derivative increasing from zero to one on the positive side. Set F=max(|x|,a(y),|z|)+|z| on X. It is an ambient convex restriction with -3/2<=F-gamma<=0. Along 1<y<2,z=0 it is quadratic, hence not finite PA.

For N=2^n linearly interpolate rational values a(1+j/N), reflect evenly and keep flat and outer linear pieces. Increasing interval slopes are k_j=(j+1/2)/N. Initial/final jumps are 1/(2N), internal jumps 1/N. Dyadic chord refinements decrease; their exact chord error on [t_j,t_{j+1}] is (t-t_j)(t_{j+1}-t)/2, maximum 1/(8N^2). Thus F_N=max(|x|,a_N(y),|z|)+|z| decreases uniformly to F with exactly that error. Coefficients and equality walls are rational; these are relative real PA PC, so F is genuinely real regularizable and n4 supplies its independent extended operator.

The horizontal plane always contributes 12 delta_0. On the positive vertical side let t_j=1+j/N, b_j=a_N(t_j), Delta_j=k_j-k_{j-1}, k_-1=0,k_N=1. At (1,0) the raw atom is 6 Delta_0. Its first weights are central 4, outward 2 and graph weights 1/q in primitive directions (q,+/-p), k0=p/q; weighted directions balance, and slopes give 0+2k0+2k0+2k0. For j>=1 the atoms are 4 Delta_j at (t_j,0), and Delta_j at each (t_j,+/-b_j). At the axis vertex first weights are 2 on both axis sides and Delta_j on both vertical sides; slopes -k_{j-1},k_j,1,1 give 4 Delta_j. At an upper graph vertex first directions (-q_left,-p_left),(q_right,p_right),(0,-1), weights 1/q_left,1/q_right,Delta_j balance as (-1,-k_left)+(1,k_right)+(0,-Delta_j)=0. Slopes -2p_left,2p_right,-1 give Delta_j. The lower vertex is reflected. For slope p/q in lowest terms, a Bezout primitive normal with determinant -1 against tangent (q,p) evaluates gradient jump (p/q,-1) to 1/q; vertical kink normals are +/-e_y and horizontal normals +/-e_z. Other walls are affine zero-weight subdivisions. Reflect atoms to negative y. Their total is 12+2*6 sum Delta_j=24.

Endpoint half-jumps vanish and remaining dyadic sums converge to Riemann integrals. Consequently the genuine sequence-independent measure is
MA_R(F)=12 delta_0 + sum_{s=+/-1} integral_1^2 [4 delta_(0,s t,0)+delta_(0,s t,(t-1)^2/2)+delta_(0,s t,-(t-1)^2/2)] dt.
These are parameter pushforward measures, not arc-length densities. Total mass is 24; moments include integral y^2=28 and integral z^2=1/5.

Let U=F-gamma+(1/4-rho)_+ and similarly U_N. The U_N are bounded real PA, uniformly converging to bounded continuous non-PA U. Inside the roof all F_N and F have exactly the same PA germ as n2: flat opposing-y endpoints force q(0)<=0, rational radial chords force q<=F, and shrinking rational simplices extend the bound without assuming q continuous. Outside the roof the obstacle bounds q by F. Since F is a competitor, its unrestricted envelope is F. Its only roof mass is 12 at zero, giving exact real contact -3. Operator stability independently gives the same limit from PA endpoint integrals. Endpoint and obstacle retain mixed differences -1/4 and +1/4 on the cross-times-z coordinates.

No literal measure is assigned to F. On y in [5/4,7/4] at z=0, the quadratic's left half increment is 3/32 and right is 5/32, both half lengths 1/4. A literal convex approximant has monotone integral slopes. If its midpoint right slope is <=0, the left increment is <=0; if >=1, the right increment is >=8/32. Either gives 2 error>=3/32, hence uniform error>=3/64 and excludes literal regularization.

Exact finite raw checks for N=1,2,4 exhaust respectively 120,364,1540 active triples, 17,27,47 primitive walls and 8,14,26 positive vertices; all agree with recursive formulas. There are 1,143 finite dyadic error cases through N=64. These checks do not prove the continuum extension or envelope. notes.summary: Reconstructed noncompact literal regularity obstruction: every positive-growth literal reference on a finite noncompact rational space fails the all-PA-obstacle antecedent. This is a regularity result, not a measure at a nonregularizable endpoint.
notes.detailedSummary: Integral norm cones matching fractional vertex gaps yield a bounded literal obstacle with exact fractional-slope envelope and a positive approximation gap. Balancing is unnecessary. In the fixed globally embedded finite positive-balanced category, caller B225 makes every positive-dimensional support noncompact, so literal pair-level orthogonality has no such regularity domain. Abstract compact charts and the unresolved real sector remain separate.
notes.text:
This reconstructs a dossier result rather than importing it as a grant. Let X be any noncompact finite rational embedded polyhedral space and gamma literal PA PC positive at infinity. Choose rational x in a noncompact connected component, rational C>gamma(x), phi=max(gamma,C) and D=phi-gamma. D is nonnegative literal PA with compact support. Refine into pointed rational cells carrying these functions. An unbounded cell has D=0: bounded affinity gives zero recession slope, and values along a recession ray eventually vanish. Since the chosen component is connected through cells and D changes from positive to zero, some bounded positive-dimensional cell sigma has nonzero integral linear part k of D. Choose primitive w in its saturated lattice with k(w)!=0 and rational segment I=x0+[0,L]w in relint(sigma). For integer N>|k(w)|, f=gamma+D/N is real rational-affine PC with bounded relative growth.

Construct a literal obstacle matching its values. For each carrying vertex v choose one sufficiently large integer M so C_v(y)=D(v)/N+M rho(y-v)>=D(y)/N on all X. On cells incident to v finite slopes bound the ratio; nonincident closed cells have positive distance from v and D is bounded. The finite vertex set permits a common integer M. Then u_N=min(D,min_v C_v) is bounded literal PA with rational walls, D/N<=u_N<=D, equals D(v)/N at vertices and vanishes on unbounded cells. Thus f is below gamma+u_N and is a competitor.

For any competitor q, q(v)<=f(v). For a rational point y of a pointed cell use a rational vertex-plus-recession representation y=sum alpha_v v+sum beta_r r, sum alpha=1. This decomposition follows from caller R230's rational finite-cone argument applied to the homogenized finite rational pointed cell. Choose v0 with alpha_v0>0 and large rational T so sum beta/T<alpha_v0. Replace that portion of v0's weight by beta_r/T at endpoints v0+Tr. These are actual rational endpoints in the same cell; obstacle and f agree there, since D=0 on its unbounded part. Jensen gives exactly q(y)<=f(y). A bounded cell uses its vertex combination alone. Shrinking rational simplices extend the bound to real points. Hence the unrestricted envelope is f.

Its primitive slope on I is gamma_sigma(w)+k(w)/N, a noninteger q0. A literal PA PC approximant has nondecreasing integral slopes on I by contained-segment Jensen and continuity. At the midpoint its right slope is either <=floor(q0) or >=ceil(q0). Comparing the left or right half increments gives uniform error >=L dist(q0,Z)/4>0. Thus f is not literally regularizable; no literal MA is assigned.

Caller B225's compact-support theorem applies exactly to nonempty finite pure strictly positive balanced cycles of dimension >=1 globally embedded in one real vector space. Those supports are noncompact, so the preceding obstruction removes every positive-growth literal pair in this fixed source category from the all-PA-obstacle regularity antecedent of source orthogonality. This does not claim a contact measure at the excluded endpoint. In dimension zero a finite rational set has pointwise envelope gamma+u and zero-fold measure [X], with zero gap. Abstract compact locally charted spaces require the separate bounded-decomposition and compatible-lattice hypotheses of caller B225/R230; no embedded compact positive-dimensional cycle is asserted. Original real-category classification is unaffected.
